name: quality
description: Overall code readability, maintainability, and structure

metrics.question: How clearly do the names of the functions, types, and variables declared in this file communicate their purpose?
rubric: Most names are cryptic, misleading, or single letters outside tiny scopes; a reader must study the implementation to guess what things are for.
Many names are vague (data, tmp, handle, doStuff) or inconsistent, so intent is often unclear without reading the body.
Names are mostly understandable, but several are generic, abbreviated, or don't match what the code actually does.
Nearly every name describes its purpose clearly, with only a few vague or inconsistent spots.
Every name states its role precisely and consistently; the code reads without comments explaining what things are.
metrics.applies_when: The file declares its own named functions, methods, types, or variables, rather than consisting only of module declarations, re-exports, imports, or plain data and configuration.

metrics.question: Does the file contain dead code?

rubric.true: The file contains commented-out code blocks, unreachable statements, or private functions or variables that are never used. Public items that other files may use do not count.
rubric.false: All code in the file is reachable, and every private item is used somewhere in the file.

metrics.question: How complex is the control flow of the code in this file?

rubric.low: Functions are short and straightforward, with little nesting and few branches.
rubric.medium: Some functions have several branches or loops, or two to three levels of nesting, but each is still easy to follow.
rubric.high: Several functions have deep nesting, long branch chains, or many interacting conditions that make them hard to follow.
rubric.critical: Control flow is tangled: very long functions with deeply nested, interdependent conditions that are hard to reason about or change safely.

metrics.question: How focused is this file on a single responsibility? Work the file delegates to other components counts as outside its responsibility, not against it.
rubric: The file mixes many unrelated responsibilities (for example I/O, business rules, formatting, and configuration) with no clear central purpose.
The file has a main purpose but also carries several unrelated concerns that belong elsewhere.
The file mostly serves one purpose, with one or two parts that would fit better in another module.
Everything in the file serves one clear purpose, apart from at most a small, loosely related helper.
The file has one sharply defined responsibility and every element directly supports it.
metrics.applies_when: The file contains its own logic or definitions (functions, methods, or types), rather than consisting only of module declarations, re-exports, or plain data and configuration.
